Generalize quasi-identifiers across datasets

Source: R/anon_generalize.R
anon_generalize.Rd

Applies generalization rules (anon_band(), anon_round(), anon_fold()) to columns and test results of linked datasets, to bring the re-identification risk measured by anon_risk() down. Every column keeps its type, class and attributes, and the data keeps its rows in the same order, so code tested on the generalized copy still runs on the original.

Usage

anon_generalize(data, rules, key = "USUBJID", keep_secrets = FALSE)

Arguments

data

A data frame, a named list of data frames linked by key, or the result of an earlier step such as anon_subject_ids().

rules

A list of rules. Elements named by a dataset are named lists of rules for that dataset's columns, as in list(dm = list(AGE = anon_band(5, top = 90), RACE = anon_fold(12, "OTHER"))); the rule applies to the column in every row. Unnamed elements are anon_rule() pairs of an anon_quasi_values() specification and a rule, which apply to every row of the test and keep its text results consistent. For a single data frame, a named list of rules by column, such as list(AGE = anon_band(5)), is enough.

key

Name of the subject identifier column, used by anon_fold() to count subjects.

keep_secrets

Logical. If TRUE, keep which categories were folded, with their numbers of subjects; read them with anon_secrets() (table generalize_folded). Default FALSE: they appear nowhere, because the names of small categories are themselves rare values.

Value

An object of class "anon_deid_step", as for anon_subject_ids().

Details

A column listed for several datasets (such as AGE in dm and in an ADaM adsl) is generalized in each dataset where it is listed, and only there: list every dataset that holds it. anon_fold() rules with the same parameters on columns of the same name count subjects across all those datasets together, so the same categories are folded everywhere.

Rules apply to the columns of the datasets themselves. Data frames nested in them (packed columns and list columns, see anon_subject_ids()) are not generalized. A warning names the datasets with the key that hold a generalized column under the same name without a rule for it.

A birth date more precise than a year (BRTHDTC, or a Date BRTHDT) in a dataset whose AGE is generalized gives the age back with a reference date such as RFSTDTC, even after the dates are offset: a warning names it. Remove birth dates or reduce them to the year. Other dates and derived columns can give a quasi-identifier back the same way (see anon_suppress()).

The log has one row per dataset, column and test, counting the values changed; it holds no values, and the settings record the rules. The step can be chained with anon_subject_ids(), anon_subject_dates() and anon_suppress() in any order: rules name columns, which those steps don't rename (unless the names hold keys or dates).

Generalized values are representatives (a band's lower bound or midpoint, a rounded number, a folded category), not the subjects' real values. Tell whoever uses the data, for example with the log in a report.

See also

generalize_rules, anon_rule(), anon_risk(), anon_suppress()

Examples

dm <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = sprintf("S%02d", 1:6),
  AGE = c(34, 37, 52, 58, 91, 93),
  RACE = c("WHITE", "WHITE", "WHITE", "ASIAN", "WHITE", "WHITE")
)
vs <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = rep(dm$USUBJID, each = 2),
  VSTESTCD = "WEIGHT",
  VSORRES = c("70.4", "71.0", "65.2", "66.0", "80.9", "79.5",
              "150.2", "151.0", "60.3", "60.0", "55.5", "56.1"),
  VSORRESU = rep(c("kg", "kg", "kg", "kg", "LB", "kg"), each = 2),
  VSSTRESC = c("70.4", "71.0", "65.2", "66.0", "80.9", "79.5",
               "68.13", "68.49", "60.3", "60.0", "55.5", "56.1"),
  VSSTRESN = c(70.4, 71.0, 65.2, 66.0, 80.9, 79.5, 68.13, 68.49, 60.3, 60.0, 55.5, 56.1),
  VSSTRESU = "kg"
)
result <- anon_generalize(
  list(dm = dm, vs = vs),
  rules = list(
    dm = list(AGE = anon_band(10, top = 90), RACE = anon_fold(2, "OTHER")),
    anon_rule(anon_quasi_values("vs", "VSTESTCD", "WEIGHT", "VSSTRESN"), anon_round(0))
  )
)
result$data$dm

#> 4     S04  50 OTHER
